# Dimension 7 — Observability

What happens to an existing OTel stack when Claude Code is replaced by Codex.
Source details in [citations](../citations.md).

Added 2026-08-21 as a seventh dimension after the original six were complete.
Same fetch date; search-backend availability had degraded by this point (see
[Gaps](#gaps-and-limitations)).

## Headline

Both tools export OpenTelemetry. **Neither exports metrics your existing
dashboards would recognise after the switch**, because the two vendors use
disjoint proprietary namespaces — `claude_code.*` and `codex.*` — and the OTel
GenAI semantic conventions that would have unified them are still at
`Development` stability with no tagged release.

Three things are worse in Codex and one is better:

| | Claude Code | Codex |
|---|---|---|
| Direct cost metric | **Yes** — `claude_code.cost.usage`, unit `USD` [71] | **None found** [3][75] |
| Session identifier on metrics | **Yes** — `session.id` by default, toggleable [71] | **Not in the documented default tag set** [3] |
| Per-event attribute schema | Fully documented [71] | Event list is "Representative", no attribute schema [3] |
| Default metrics destination | your collector, or none | **`statsig`** — an OpenAI-side default [1][74] |
| Config surface | ~30 env vars [71] | one `[otel]` TOML block [1][3] |
| Docs-vs-source agreement | not checked | **20 metrics in source are undocumented** [3][75] |

The one thing that is better: Codex's config is a single TOML block rather than
thirty environment variables, and it is admin-enforceable through
`requirements.toml` in a way Claude Code's exporter selectors are not [1][71].

## 1. Claude Code's surface, for the record

Everything here from [71] unless noted. The page states no publication date;
it dates itself through version gates such as "Requires Claude Code v2.1.232 or
later".

**Enable:** `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1`, plus at least one exporter [72].
Selectors: `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER` (`console|otlp|prometheus|none`),
`OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER`, `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER` (beta).

**Protocols:** `grpc`, `http/json`, `http/protobuf`. Directly relevant to a
CONNECT-proxy sandbox:

> "Claude Code has no default protocol, so set this or the signal-specific
> protocol variable for each `otlp` exporter you enable." [71]

> "For the `http/protobuf` and `http/json` protocols, Claude Code sends each
> export request with a `Content-Length` header." [71]

**The eight metrics** [71]:

| Metric | Unit | Notable attributes |
|---|---|---|
| `claude_code.session.count` | — | `start_type` (`fresh`/`resume`/`continue`/`agents_view`) |
| `claude_code.lines_of_code.count` | — | `type` (`added`/`removed`), `model` |
| `claude_code.pull_request.count` | — | — |
| `claude_code.commit.count` | — | — |
| `claude_code.cost.usage` | `USD` | `model`, `query_source`, `speed`, `effort`, `agent.name`, `skill.name`, `plugin.name`, `mcp_server.name`, `mcp_tool.name` |
| `claude_code.token.usage` | `tokens` | `type` (`input`/`output`/`cacheRead`/`cacheCreation`), `model`, plus the same attribution set |
| `claude_code.code_edit_tool.decision` | — | `tool_name`, `decision`, `source`, `language` |
| `claude_code.active_time.total` | `s` | `type` (`user`/`cli`) |

Caveat: "When `prometheus` is the only exporter listed in
`OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER`, Claude Code omits the `USD`, `tokens`, and `s` units."
[71]

**Events** are a much longer list — `claude_code.user_prompt`,
`claude_code.assistant_response`, `claude_code.tool_result`,
`claude_code.api_request`, `claude_code.api_error`, `claude_code.tool_decision`,
`claude_code.hook_execution_start`/`_complete`, `claude_code.compaction`,
`claude_code.subagent_completed` and more — each with a documented attribute
set [71]. Meter name: `com.anthropic.claude_code` [71].

**Cardinality toggles** (the reason this matters is billing, not tidiness):

| Variable | Controls | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_SESSION_ID` | `session.id` | `true` |
| `OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_VERSION` | `app.version` | `false` |
| `OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_ACCOUNT_UUID` | `user.account_uuid`, `user.account_id` | `true` |
| `OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_ENTRYPOINT` | `app.entrypoint` | `false` |
| `OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` | `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` keys as datapoint attributes | `true` |

A known limitation, from Anthropic's own tracker: the session-ID toggle cannot
be split between signals. Issue #70210, opened 2026-06-23, **closed as not
planned**, labelled stale [88]:

> "This is immensely helpful in events/logs, but causes high cardinality in
> metrics. I'd love to turn this on for logs but turn it off for metrics." [88]

**Privacy toggles**, all off by default: `OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS`,
`OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES`, `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS`,
`OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT`, `OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES` [71].

**Tracing is beta**, gated behind `CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1`:
"Tracing is in beta. Span names and attributes may change between releases."
[72]

**Admin enforcement is partial** — worth knowing before assuming parity:

> "When you set an `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` variable in managed settings, Claude
> Code removes conflicting developer-set variables at startup and logs a
> warning… `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER`, `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER`, and the beta
> `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER` follow normal per-key precedence. A developer's setting
> can still disable a signal or switch it to the console exporter." [71]

Also: "Claude Code doesn't pass `OTEL_*` environment variables to the
subprocesses it spawns." [71]

## 2. Codex's surface

**Config is TOML, not environment variables.** The `[otel]` block [1][3]:

```toml
[otel]
environment = "staging"        # default: "dev"
exporter = "none"              # none | otlp-http | otlp-grpc
log_user_prompt = false
metrics_exporter = "statsig"   # none | statsig | otlp-http | otlp-grpc
trace_exporter = "none"        # none | otlp-http | otlp-grpc

[otel]
exporter = { otlp-http = { endpoint = "https://otel.example.com/v1/logs",
                           protocol = "binary",
                           headers = { "x-otlp-api-key" = "${OTLP_TOKEN}" } }}
```

Per-exporter sub-keys: `.endpoint`, `.headers`, `.protocol` (`binary | json`),
`.tls.ca-certificate`, `.tls.client-certificate`, `.tls.client-private-key` [1].
The crate additionally documents `[otel.span_attributes]` and
`[otel.tracestate.<member>]`, which do **not** appear in the config-reference
key list [74].

**Two facts that matter for a proxied sandbox.** OTLP/HTTP is a first-class
exporter for logs, traces and metrics [1][3][74] — so the gRPC-can't-traverse-
CONNECT constraint is satisfiable. And `otel` is on the ten-key project-scope
ignore list, so telemetry routing must live in the user-level
`~/.codex/config.toml` [1][3].

**Reusing existing collector plumbing will not work as-is.** Codex's published
environment-variable list contains twelve entries and **none of them is an
`OTEL_*` variable** [15]. The `[otel]` TOML block is the documented path.

**Default metrics destination is not your collector.** `otel.metrics_exporter`
"defaults to `statsig`" [1], and the crate describes `OtelExporter::Statsig` as
"a shorthand for exporting OTLP/HTTP JSON metrics to Statsig using
Codex-internal defaults" [74]. This is a separate switch from `analytics.enabled`
(§3) and must be explicitly repointed.

**Events** — the catalogue is `codex.conversation_starts`, `codex.api_request`,
`codex.sse_event`, `codex.websocket_request`, `codex.websocket_event`,
`codex.user_prompt`, `codex.tool_decision`, `codex.tool_result` [3]. The page
calls these "Representative event types", i.e. **not exhaustive**, and unlike
Claude Code it publishes no per-event attribute schema [3]. Any event-level
Codex dashboard spec is therefore partly guesswork.

**Default metric tags:** "Each metric below also includes default metadata tags:
`auth_mode`, `originator`, `session_source`, `model`, and `app.version`" [3].

Independent corroboration that this pipeline is real and consumed in
production, from AWS [86]:

> "OpenAI Codex emits OpenTelemetry (OTel) metrics about token usage, per-turn
> latency, API requests, tool calls, and approvals… Codex configures its metrics
> exporter through the `[otel]` section of its `config.toml` file." [86]

And from OpenAI's own security blog, dated 2026-05-08 [87]:

> "Codex supports OpenTelemetry log export for various Codex events such as
> user prompts, tool approval decisions, tool execution results, MCP server
> usage, and network proxy allow or deny events." [87]

### Documentation is behind the source

Diffing `codex-rs/otel/src/metrics/names.rs` (54 constants, all `codex.`-prefixed)
[75] against the documented metrics catalogue [3] gives divergence in both
directions.

Divergence *documented-but-not-in-source* is expected and explained — the docs
say "Most metric names are centralized in `codex-rs/otel/src/metrics/names.rs`;
feature-specific metrics emitted outside that file are included here too" [3].

Divergence the other way is the finding. **Twenty metric names exist in source
and appear nowhere in the documentation** [3][75]:

`codex.artifact.operation.started`, `codex.artifact.operation.expected_output_count`,
`codex.process.start`, `codex.turn.unified_exec.running_processes`,
`codex.guardian.review`, `codex.guardian.review.duration_ms`,
`codex.guardian.review.ttft.duration_ms`, `codex.guardian.review.token_usage`,
`codex.goal.created`, `codex.goal.resumed`, `codex.goal.completed`,
`codex.goal.budget_limited`, `codex.goal.usage_limited`, `codex.goal.blocked`,
`codex.goal.token_count`, `codex.goal.duration_s`,
`codex.plugins.install_elicitation.sent`, `codex.plugins.install_suggestion`,
`codex.startup.phase.duration_ms`,
`codex.thread.skills.description_truncated_chars`.

**Caveat, and it is a real one:** `names.rs` was read from the `main` branch,
not a release tag [75]. These constants may be ahead of any shipped build, or
feature-flagged, or dead. Their presence is evidence the docs are not a complete
inventory; it is not evidence that a shipped Codex emits them.

Two internal inconsistencies on the documentation page itself, both quoted
verbatim from [3]:

1. The *metric* names are `codex.websocket.request` and `codex.websocket.event`
   (dots), while the *event* names on the same page are
   `codex.websocket_request` and `codex.websocket_event` (underscores).
2. An "OTel metrics emitted" table lists **10** metrics; a "Metrics catalog"
   further down the same page lists roughly **90**. The page never reconciles
   the two.

## 3. Codex's second telemetry stream

Distinct from OTel and on by default:

> "By default, Codex periodically sends a small amount of anonymous usage and
> health data back to OpenAI… These metrics don't contain any personally
> identifiable information (PII). **Metrics collection is independent of OTel
> log/trace export.**" [3]

Disable:

```toml
[analytics]
enabled = false
```

The config-reference row reads: `analytics.enabled`, boolean, "Enable or disable
analytics for this machine/profile. When unset, the client default applies" [1].

**On a practitioner claim this research checked and partly rejected.**
`codexinsider.com` asserts "Two official pages, two different stories on what
happens when you don't set it" [91]. Reading both pages directly: config-advanced
states the runtime default in prose [3]; config-reference states no contradictory
default and defers with "When unset, the client default applies" [1]. That is
**silence in one source plus a stated default in the other, not a contradiction**.
The site's operational advice — treat unset as on — is correct; its framing as a
documented conflict is not supported.

The default is independently confirmed by an OpenAI maintainer [76]:

> "**Analytics will default to enabled, except in jurisdictions where opt-out is
> required by law.** You will be able to explicitly disable analytics via a new
> analytics feature flag." [76]

That jurisdictional carve-out is what "the client default applies" is deferring
to. The same thread gives examples of what is collected — "list of experimental
feature used / number of `/review` done / number of approval request
approved/refused / average tool call duration" — and confirms admin control:

> "Enterprise plan admins can choose to disable analytics for all users in their
> organization using managed config overrides." [76]

**For a sandbox with a hostname allowlist this is operationally relevant twice
over:** `analytics.enabled = false` and repointing `otel.metrics_exporter` away
from `statsig` are two separate switches, and leaving either at its default
means outbound traffic to an OpenAI-side destination that the policy would have
to allow or would silently block.

## 4. The GenAI semantic conventions do not rescue this

The hope would be that both vendors emit `gen_ai.*` names and a
convention-based dashboard survives the switch. They do not, and the convention
is not ready either.

**Current home.** The conventions moved out of the core semconv repository
[83][84]:

> "GenAI semantic conventions have moved to the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic
> conventions repository. This page has moved and is no longer maintained in
> this repository." [83]

The new home is `open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai` [77], which scopes
itself as "Semantic Conventions for Generative AI (GenAI), including spans,
metrics, and events for GenAI clients, MCP (Model Context Protocol), and
provider-specific conventions (OpenAI, etc.)" [78]. Repository metadata as
fetched: 274 stars, 82 forks, 620 commits, Apache-2.0 [77]. It is an active
repository — the question is not whether work is happening but whether any of
it has stabilised.

**Current stability: `Development`, everywhere, with no release.** Two
practitioner sources in the pool make opposite claims, so this was resolved from
primary sources only:

| Evidence | Finding |
|---|---|
| `gen-ai-metrics.md` document header [79] | `**Status**: [Development][DocumentStatus]` |
| Every metric row in [79] | `Development` badge — all twelve |
| Attribute registry [80] | **118 `Development` badges, zero `Stable` badges**. The three occurrences of "stable" in that file are prose ("the unique and stable identifier of the GenAI hosted agent resource"), not stability markers |
| CHANGELOG [81] | contains only `## Unreleased` |
| Releases page [82] | **"There aren't any releases here."** |
| opentelemetry.io blog index [85] | no post announcing GenAI stabilization — while a 2023 post "HTTP semconv are stable" shows the project does announce such milestones there |

**Verdict: the primary evidence supports [89] and refutes [90].** The claim that
the SIG "has stabilized the GenAI Semantic Conventions in June 2026" [90] is
contradicted by the live specification. Its supporting detail is independently
wrong against the registry [80]: it cites `gen_ai.system` (deprecated in favour
of `gen_ai.provider.name`), `gen_ai.prompt` ("Removed, no replacement at this
time"), `usage.input_tokens`/`usage.output_tokens` (the real names are
`gen_ai.usage.*`), `gen_ai.response.finish_reason` (the real name is plural),
and `gen_ai.tool.status` (not in the registry). **No middle position is taken
here: the conventions are at Development stability as of 2026-08-21.**

This also updates the repo's own prior finding. `research/multi-agent-observability/`
(last revised 2026-04-02) recorded the GenAI conventions as "Development status"
with cost metrics having no OTEL standard. **Both still hold**, four months on —
and the conventions have additionally moved repository and still have no tagged
release.

### Conformance: partial on one side, none on the other

The conventions define twelve `gen_ai.*` metrics including
`gen_ai.client.token.usage`, and attributes including `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`,
`gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`, `gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens`,
`gen_ai.request.model`, `gen_ai.token.type`, `gen_ai.provider.name` [79][80].

**Claude Code — partial, traces only.** It emits exactly six convention names,
all on spans and each labelled "OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic convention":
`gen_ai.system`, `gen_ai.request.model`, `gen_ai.response.id`,
`gen_ai.response.finish_reasons`, `gen_ai.tool.call.id`, and the span event
`gen_ai.request.attempt` [71]. Its metrics and events conform to **none** of the
convention names — token and cost attributes are `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`,
`cache_read_tokens`, `cache_creation_tokens`, `cost_usd`, not the
`gen_ai.usage.*` forms [71]. Note also that one of the six it does emit,
`gen_ai.system`, is **deprecated** in the registry in favour of
`gen_ai.provider.name`, which Claude Code does not emit [80].

**Codex — none.** A grep for `gen_ai` returns zero hits across `names.rs`, the
crate README, config-advanced and config-reference [3][74][75]. Token attribution
is `token_type` with values `total`, `input`, `cached_input`, `output`,
`reasoning_output` [3]; the convention's attribute is `gen_ai.token.type` with
values `input`/`output` [79]. Semantically parallel, lexically disjoint.

**Practical consequence: every metric-level panel is rebuilt name-for-name.** A
dashboard keyed on `claude_code.*` carries across to Codex not at all; a
dashboard keyed on `gen_ai.*` never worked for either tool's metrics in the
first place.

## 5. Can telemetry answer "what did this session cost"?

This is the question that matters, because the
[pricing dimension](pricing-plans-quota.md) established that published pricing
cannot settle a cost comparison — so the [trial protocol](../claude-code-to-codex-transition.md#the-trial-protocol)
depends on measurement.

**Claude Code — yes, twice over.**

1. Directly: `claude_code.cost.usage`, unit `USD`, "Incremented after each API
   request", carrying `model` and the full attribution set [71]. Event
   `claude_code.api_request` carries `cost_usd` and `cost_usd_micros` [71].
2. Recomputed from your own price table: `claude_code.token.usage` carries
   `type` and `model` **on the same datapoint**, with `session.id` present by
   default [71]. Group by `session.id` × `model` × `type` and multiply.

With a caveat Anthropic states plainly [71][73]:

> "Cost metrics are approximations. For official billing data, refer to your API
> provider." [71]

> "The SDK computes them locally from a price table bundled at build time, so
> they can drift from what you are actually billed when: pricing changes / the
> installed SDK version does not recognize a model / billing rules apply that
> the client cannot model… **Do not bill end users or trigger financial
> decisions from these fields.**" [73]

Also a fixed defect worth knowing if you compare historical data: before
v2.1.214, multi-frame usage streams "inflated `claude_code.cost.usage` and
`claude_code.token.usage` by roughly one extra full request per extra frame"
[71].

**Codex — partly, and this is a regression.**

- **No cost metric exists.** A search for cost/USD across `names.rs`, the crate
  README and the documented catalogue returns nothing relevant [3][74][75].
- **Token counts and model attribution are co-located**, so external
  computation is possible: `codex.turn.token_usage` (histogram) carries
  `token_type` (`total`, `input`, `cached_input`, `output`, `reasoning_output`),
  and `model` is one of the default metadata tags on every metric [3]. Per-model,
  per-token-type spend is computable from a price table.
- **But per-session attribution is not demonstrably available from the metrics
  stream.** The documented default tags are `auth_mode`, `originator`,
  `session_source`, `model`, `app.version` [3] — `session_source` is a category,
  not an identifier. Event metadata is documented to include "conversation id"
  [3], but the metrics tag list is not. This research could not establish that
  any Codex *metric* carries a session or conversation identifier.
- Two secondary frictions: `codex.turn.token_usage` is a **histogram**, so
  summing it for billing depends on your backend retaining the sum, where
  Claude Code's `claude_code.token.usage` is a counter [3][71]; and
  `codex.sse_event` is documented as carrying "token counts on
  `response.completed`" [3] without ever naming those attributes.

**Bottom line.** Claude Code answers the cost question from telemetry alone, as
an acknowledged client-side estimate. Codex answers "what did this model cost
across turns" but, on the documented metric tag set, not "what did *this
session* cost". For a trial protocol whose Step 2 is dollars-per-completed-task,
that gap has to be closed empirically — run the trial, then check whether an
emitted metric carries a conversation identifier the docs omit.

## 6. Delta for the `openshell-sandbox` wrapper

Extends the table in
[openshell-sandbox-implications](openshell-sandbox-implications.md).
Local facts are marked *(local)*.

| Today *(local)* | With Codex | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY` + `OTEL_*` env vars in `/sandbox/.env` | `[otel]` block in user-level `~/.codex/config.toml` — **no `OTEL_*` env var path exists** [15] | Rewrite, different mechanism |
| Dummy OTEL hooks (`python3 -c ""`) forcing emission | Delete — Codex emits natively [3] | Deletion |
| OTLP HTTP on 4318 through the CONNECT proxy *(local gotcha 13)* | Same constraint, and satisfiable — `otlp-http` with `protocol = "binary"` [1][3][87] | None |
| `otel` policy block allows one collector host *(local)* | Add nothing **if** you also set `analytics.enabled = false` and repoint `otel.metrics_exporter` off `statsig`; otherwise an OpenAI-side host must be allowed [1][74] | Two config lines, or a policy entry |
| `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` carries `sandbox.profile` *(local)* | `[otel.span_attributes]` [74] and `otel.environment` [1] are the nearest levers | Rework |
| Dashboards keyed on `claude_code.*` | Rebuild against `codex.*` [3][71][75] | **The real cost of this dimension** |

One unresolved risk specific to this setup: Claude Code documents that it sends
a `Content-Length` header on `http/protobuf` and `http/json` exports [71] — a
detail that exists because some proxies reject chunked encoding. **No Codex
source in this pool states whether its OTLP/HTTP exporter does the same.**
Through a CONNECT proxy that is a live unknown, and cheap to test.

## Gaps and limitations

1. **Search was effectively single-engine for this dimension.** The health probe
   reported 2 of 7 backends alive (`wikipedia`, `yahoo`) with a suggested list of
   `yahoo` alone. All 12 queries returned `single_wave: true`, with the
   `wikipedia` wave failing on every one. There is no cross-engine corroboration
   for any result in this batch. Several high-value sources ([71], [79]–[82])
   were reached by direct URL rather than by search.
2. **Does any Codex metric carry a session or conversation identifier?** Not
   resolvable from these sources, and it decides whether per-session cost is
   answerable. This is the single most important open question in the dimension.
3. **`names.rs` is `main`-branch** [75]. The 20 undocumented metric names may not
   exist in any shipped build.
4. **Codex's event catalogue is self-described as "Representative"** [3] and has
   no per-event attribute schema, so it cannot be treated as complete.
5. **The exact token-count attribute names on `codex.sse_event` are never
   enumerated** [3].
6. Whether Codex's OTLP/HTTP exporter sets `Content-Length` is unstated in every
   Codex source read.
7. `code.claude.com/docs/en/administration` returned 404 [92]; the admin
   enforcement behaviour was found on [71] instead, so this is not material.
8. The `praesidia.ai` attribution of the conventions' move to "v1.42.0 / June
   2026" [89] is **not** corroborated by any primary source here — the move is
   confirmed [83][84], its version and date are not.
9. Claude Code's detailed `claude_code.hook` span requires
   `ENABLE_BETA_TRACING_DETAILED=1`, `BETA_TRACING_ENDPOINT`, and in interactive
   CLI sessions "your organization to be allowlisted for the feature" [71].
   Whether an individual can obtain that is unaddressed.
